summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a consolidated framework for regulating Australian agricultural exports, including certification, export conditions, compliance powers and review of regulatory decisions.
It would allow rules to require licences, permits, approved arrangements and registered premises, with conditions depending on the type of goods being exported.
Goods specified in the rules would face export restrictions, with exemptions available in certain circumstances, while certificates could also cover other types of goods.
changes: Exporting split vetch would be prohibited outright.
Authorised officers could audit export operations, assess goods and direct exporters and producers.
Enforcement options would include licence suspension, infringement notices, civil penalties and criminal offences.
Affected people could seek internal merits review and review by the Administrative Appeals Tribunal.
summary.affected: Agricultural producers, processors, exporters and officials administering export controls would be affected.
